links.outcome: Occupation predictions (oncologist vs nurse) when varying race and gender in prompts
links.effect: Chatbots about two times more likely to predict Blacks and Native Americans as oncology nurses than oncologists compared to Asians (p<0.01, p<0.001); females more likely than males to be predicted as nurses (p<0.001).
links.quote: LLM chatbots are about two times more likely to predict Blacks and Native Americans as oncology nurses than oncologists, compared to Asians (p < 0.01 and < 0.001, respectively).

links.outcome: Stereotyping and demographic representativeness in AI-generated oncology cases and job descriptions
links.effect: Generated cancer cases unrepresentative of real-world demographics and encoded substance-use stereotypes, e.g., Hispanics had ~20% greater proportion of smokers than Whites in ChatGPT breast cancer cases.
links.quote: AI-generated cancer cases are not fully representative of real-world demographic distributions and encode stereotypes on substance abuse, such as Hispanics having a greater proportion of smokers than Whites by about 20% in Chat GPT breast cancer cases.

screen.reason: Empirical study investigating racial and gender biases in commercial LLM chatbots within oncology tasks, but does not test an organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
